haiku-low.q1: Held for 10 minutes from creation. If not claimed in time, a timer sets the hold to RELEASED and the stock goes back on sale. The order keeps waiting for the webhook.
haiku-low.q2: Before charging. Inventory reserves all lines in one transaction first. If any line is short, nothing is reserved, Payment is never called, and the customer is told which items are short.
haiku-low.q3: Every charge request carries the order id as its idempotency key. On a re-send, the provider returns the original result instead of charging again.
haiku-low.q4: Order is cancelled as CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK and Payment requests a full refund, with the customer emailed. Refund retries until accepted, or ends on the FAILED_NEEDS_ATTENTION manual list.
haiku-low.q5: Cart is emptied only when it receives the OrderConfirmed event, which empties it entirely. On any failure the cart is never emptied and stays unchanged for retry.
haiku-low.q6: The Order service owns and moves order status and decides the next step. The status and order record are stored in Order's own database, with order id, status, and frozen lines.
haiku-low.q7: The provider sends a webhook to Payment. Payment records it and publishes PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined on the shared broker, which Order consumes.
haiku-low.q8: Webhooks are deduplicated by provider event id under a unique constraint; a repeat returns 200 and stops. Consumers apply changes only from an allowed previous status, so re-delivered broker messages are harmless.
haiku-low.q9: Payment publishes PaymentDeclined, Order cancels and publishes OrderCancelled, and Inventory releases the hold. If the hold already lapsed, the release does nothing.
haiku-low.q10: Order asks Inventory to claim the stock. If the hold is no longer HELD, the claim is refused, and Order cancels and requests a full refund. A successful claim leads to fulfilment.
haiku-low.q11: The refund stays PENDING and is retried with backoff, never deleted. After the retry limit it becomes FAILED_NEEDS_ATTENTION, operations are alerted, and it stays on a manual retry list. Payment's refund record tracks it.
haiku-low.q12: The OrderConfirmed event, published by Order after the claim succeeds, causes the Cart service to empty the cart entirely.

sonnet.q1: 10 minutes (expires_at = created + 10 min). If not claimed, a timer sets the hold to RELEASED and the stock goes back on sale.
sonnet.q2: Reserved before charging (reserve, then AWAITING_PAYMENT, then charge). If any line is short, nothing is reserved, Order replies with the short items, Payment is never called, and the cart stays unchanged.
sonnet.q3: The idempotency key (the order id) on every charge request; the provider returns the original result instead of charging again.
sonnet.q4: Inventory refuses the claim, Order sets CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK, requests a full refund from Payment and emails the customer (out of stock, refund coming). The money is refunded, retried until REFUNDED or put on the FAILED_NEEDS_ATTENTION list.
sonnet.q5: The cart is emptied only when Cart receives the OrderConfirmed event. On any failure it is left exactly as it was, so the customer can retry.
sonnet.q6: The Order service owns the status and decides what happens next, moving it via HTTP calls, replies and events. The record is the order's status field in Order's own database (PENDING, AWAITING_PAYMENT, PAID_PENDING_CLAIM, CONFIRMED, etc.).
sonnet.q7: The provider sends a webhook to Payment, which records the outcome and publishes a PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined event on the broker (via an outbox and relay); Order consumes that event.
sonnet.q8: Payment stores the provider event id under a unique constraint, written in the same transaction as the state change. A repeat finds the id, replies 200 OK and does nothing. Consumers also apply status changes only from an allowed previous status, so re-delivered broker messages are harmless.
sonnet.q9: Inventory releases the hold and the stock goes back on sale. This is triggered by the OrderCancelled event that Order publishes after receiving PaymentDeclined. If the hold already lapsed, the release does nothing.
sonnet.q10: Order asks Inventory to claim the hold, using an atomic HELD to CLAIMED update. If the hold is still HELD, the claim succeeds and the order is confirmed. If it was already released, the claim is refused, the order is cancelled out of stock, and a full refund is requested.
sonnet.q11: The refund stays PENDING and is retried with backoff (the same refund idempotency key is reused). After max attempts it becomes FAILED_NEEDS_ATTENTION, operations are alerted, and it stays on a manual retry list, never deleted. It is tracked in Payment's database refund record (status, attempt count, next retry time, last error).
sonnet.q12: The OrderConfirmed event, published by Order when the order reaches CONFIRMED, causes the Cart service to empty the cart.
